text:
B: Hi, can you hear me?
A: Yes, I can. Hello. Lee.
B: Jasmine. Hi Lee.
A: Where are you calling from?
B: Plymouth. You?
A: Hucknall, near Nottingham.
B: Okay. I like your background, by the way. Very organised. The folders by year.
A: Er, thank you. Habit, really. I'm in quality, so it sort of comes with the job.
B: What's quality, like inspection?
A: Yes. Aerospace parts. I measure them on a CMM, that's a coordinate measuring machine, and if something's out of spec I write it up. And I keep the calibration records. When there's an audit coming, they tend to come to me.
B: Honestly, you looked like an accountant in your photo. You'd get on with my accountant.
A: I do the household budget in Excel, so maybe.
B: Proper. I do my books in Xero. I've got two bubble tea shops, franchise ones, in the city centre.
A: Two. How long have you had them?
B: First one 2019, then 2022 the second. I want a third, maybe Exeter.
A: That's a fair bit of risk, I'd say.
B: Bit, yeah. One nearly closed one winter. It was really slow, January, February, nobody wants cold drinks. I was more worried than I told anyone, to be fair. But it came back. Summer saved it.
A: Seasonal, then.
B: Very. You can forecast it, though. I do the stock by the weather, basically.
A: That's sensible.
B: Do you do audits yourself, or they audit you?
A: They audit us. Customer audits, and the certification body. Last one was March. Sorry, April. Early April.
B: And you pass?
A: We passed, yes. No major findings.
B: I'd hate that. Somebody going through all my paperwork.
A: It's fine if it's done properly in the first place.
B: That's the thing. Mine's mostly done properly.
A: Mostly.
B: Mostly, lah. Nobody checks the cleaning log for the fridges, you know.
A: Somebody will, one day.
B: Yeah, yeah. Okay. You sound like my supervisor. Do you have kids?
A: Two. My son's twenty-four, he's in Arnold with his girlfriend. My daughter's twenty, she's at university in Sheffield.
B: Oh nice. What's she studying?
A: Er, psychology. She comes back some weekends. House is quiet when she's not there, to be fair. We've turned my son's old room into an office.
B: That's where you are now?
A: That's where I am now, yes.
B: I came here for uni as well. From Malaysia, when I was eighteen. My mum was worried the whole time. She still calls every Sunday.
A: I'd say that's normal. You don't stop worrying.
B: She'd agree with you. Do you go away much?
A: Static caravan, near Mablethorpe. Same park every year.
B: Every year? I couldn't. I like all-inclusive. Tenerife, Turkey. Pool, nice hotel, don't have to cook.
A: We did Majorca for our twenty-fifth. It was nice. But you know where everything is at the caravan.
B: Fair. I get that. Same as going back home, I suppose.
A: Yes. Sort of the same thing.
